content: Methyldopa is prescribed to manage high blood pressure. It belongs to a class of medications known as antihypertensives. This drug functions by relaxing the blood vessels, allowing blood to flow more easily throughout the body. Methyldopa is available in tablet and liquid forms for oral administration. It is typically taken two to four times daily. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take methyldopa exactly as directed. Do not take more or less of it or take it more frequently than prescribed by your doctor. If you are using the liquid form, shake it well before each dose to ensure the medication is evenly mixed. Use a dose-measuring spoon or cup to measure the correct amount of liquid for each dose, not a regular household spoon. Methyldopa helps control high blood pressure but does not cure it. Continue taking methyldopa even if you feel well. Do not stop taking it without consulting your doctor, as suddenly stopping the medication may cause your blood pressure to rise and lead to side effects. Your doctor will gradually reduce your dose if needed. This medication may also be prescribed for other uses. Consult your doctor or pharmacist for more information. Before taking methyldopa, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to methyldopa, any other medications, sulfites, or any of the ingredients in methyldopa tablets or liquid. Ask your doctor or pharmacist for a list of the ingredients. Inform your doctor if you are taking a monoamine oxidase (MAO) inhibitor, such as isocarboxazid (Marplan), phenelzine (Nardil), selegiline (Eldepryl, Emsam, Zelapar), or tranylcypromine (Parnate), as your doctor will likely advise against taking methyldopa. Additionally, inform your doctor and pharmacist about all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, nutritional supplements, and herbal products you are taking or plan to take. Be sure to mention medications such as haloperidol (Haldol), levodopa (Larodopa, Sinemet), lithium (Eskalith, Lithobid), other medications for high blood pressure, and tolbutamide (Orinase). Your doctor may need to adjust the doses of your medications or monitor you carefully for side effects. Avoid taking methyldopa with iron supplements or vitamins containing iron. Inform your doctor if you have or have ever had kidney or liver disease, including hepatitis or cirrhosis. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking methyldopa, contact your doctor immediately. Discuss the risks of taking methyldopa if you are 65 years of age or older, as it may not be as safe as other medications for treating the same condition. If you are undergoing surgery, including dental surgery, inform your doctor or dentist that you are taking methyldopa. Be aware that this medication may cause drowsiness. Avoid driving or operating machinery for 48–72 hours after starting methyldopa or after your dose is increased. Your doctor may recommend a low-salt or low-sodium diet. Follow these dietary instructions carefully. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to make up for a missed one. Methyldopa may cause side effects. Inform your doctor if any of these symptoms are severe or persistent: drowsiness, headache, muscle weakness, swollen ankles or feet, upset stomach, vomiting, diarrhea, gas, dry mouth, or rash. Some side effects can be serious. Contact your doctor immediately if you experience unexplained fever, extreme tiredness, or yellowing of the skin or eyes. Methyldopa may cause other side effects. Contact your doctor if you experience any unusual problems while taking this medication. If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor may report it to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store this medication in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Store tablets at room temperature, away from excess heat and moisture (not in the bathroom). The liquid form may be stored in the refrigerator or at room temperature. Dispose of any outdated or no longer needed medication. Consult your pharmacist about the proper disposal of your medication. In case of overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the victim has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory. Your blood pressure should be checked regularly to monitor your response to methyldopa. Your doctor may order specific lab tests to monitor your red blood cell count and liver function. Methyldopa may cause your urine to darken when exposed to air; this effect is harmless. Do not share your medication with others. Consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription. It is important to maintain a written list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, as well as any vitamins, minerals, or dietary supplements. Bring this list with you to each doctor’s visit or if you are admitted to a hospital. This information is also essential in case of emergencies.
